Reviewing Incident Reports

subset_review.Rmd
Function Purpose
checkSubsetIncidents() Check IDs, affected responses and design assignments.
prepareSubsetInfo() Select the reported person-response pairs.
visualSubsetRecode() Review and recode by class or person; pause and resume.

1. Inputs

Use your response data, a long incident table, and the design tables from one input list. No separate class roster is needed. Keep existing ID column names and choose the response level explicitly:

library(eatPrep)
student_id <- "learner_key"
class_id <- "group_key"
data_level <- "unit"  # Use "subunit" for original or recoded subunit columns.

The student-ID column must occur in dat, incidents and inputList$rotation; the class-ID column in dat and incidents. Student IDs must be unique, and class IDs must identify classes across schools.

Runnable example inputs (all identifiers and values are fictional) 
dat <- data.frame(
  learner_key = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E"),
  group_key = c("K1", "K1", "K1", "K2", "K2"),
  U12 = c("mbi", "1", "2", "1", NA), U3 = c("1", "mnr", "0", "1", "1")
)
inputList <- list(
  subunits = data.frame(
    subunit = c("I1", "I2", "I3"), subunitRecoded = c("I1R", "I2R", "I3R"),
    unit = c("U12", "U12", "U3")
  ),
  blocks = data.frame(
    subunit = c("I1", "I2", "I3"), block = c("b1", "b1", "b2"),
    subunitBlockPosition = c(1, 2, 1)
  ),
  booklets = data.frame(
    booklet = c("X", "Y"), block1 = c("b1", "b2"), block2 = c("b2", "b1")
  ),
  rotation = data.frame(learner_key = dat$learner_key,
                        booklet = c("X", "Y", "X", "X", "Y"))
)
incidents <- data.frame(
  group_key = c("K1", "K1", "K1", "K2"),
  learner_key = c("A", "A", "B", NA), blockPosition = c(1, 2, 1, 2),
  comment = c("Display error", "Display error", "Interrupted test", "Audio failure")
)

Each incident row names one affected block position. Keep repeated persons on separate rows. Positions refer to each person’s booklet: in this example, position 1 means block b1 for A, but b2 for B.

Person IDs within a class’s incident rows Selection
All supplied Exactly the reported person-position pairs.
All missing (NA, empty or whitespace) All members of that class in dat, at the reported positions.
Mixed supplied and missing Error: clarify the intended selection.

The example selects A at positions 1 and 2, B at position 1, and everyone in K2 at position 2. C is not selected. Optional issueId and level columns usually need not be supplied; comment is optional too.

2. Check 

checked <- checkSubsetIncidents(
  dat, incidents, booklets = inputList$booklets,
  blocks = inputList$blocks, rotation = inputList$rotation,
  subunits = inputList$subunits, dataLevel = data_level,
  ID = student_id, classID = class_id
)
checked
#> Incident check (unit responses)
#> Cases: 4 of 4 incident rows matched to dat.
#> Missing unit columns: 0 detected among 2 distinct unit identifiers checked.
#> Ready for review: 4 incident rows.
#> All incident rows could be matched and resolved.

Use distinct counts, rather than counting repeated problem records:

checked$summary[c("missingPersons", "missingClasses", "missingUnits", "readyRows")]
checked$missing  # Identifiers behind the missing counts.
print(checked, max_problems = 10)
unique(checked$ignored[c("subunit", "unit", "ignoredReason")])

$problems contains findings to inspect; $ignored lists omitted design entries without usable response columns. Preparation skips absent persons/classes by default (unmatched = "drop") and retains the report. Contradictory assignments, ambiguities affecting existing responses and unresolved reported positions still stop preparation, as does an entirely empty selection. Use unmatched = "error" for strict handling of absent cases.

The review covers the available data and reported incidents. Broader metadata checks remain separate: checkInputList() and checkDesign(). Missing-item totals are provisional when checked$summary$itemCheckComplete is FALSE.

3. Prepare and review

Use the same ID names, response level and input list for preparation:

info <- prepareSubsetInfo(
  dat, incidents = incidents, booklets = inputList$booklets,
  blocks = inputList$blocks, rotation = inputList$rotation,
  subunits = inputList$subunits, dataLevel = data_level,
  ID = student_id, classID = class_id
)

In unit mode, any affected subunit selects its entire unit. Here I1 and I2 both select U12, which is displayed and recoded once per person. Supply the complete inputList$subunits table; subunit names and unit response names may differ.

result <- visualSubsetRecode(
  dat, info, toRecodeVal = "mci", nonValidValues = c("mbi", "mnr"),
  positions = TRUE, comments = TRUE
)

This gives one decision per class. Different item/position layouts appear in separate tables within that decision. positions = TRUE adds the two rows below the responses and enables block selection; comments = TRUE shows incident comments. Both switches accept TRUE or FALSE. For the first class:

#>        learner_key  U12 U3
#>                  A  mbi  1
#>  ----------------- ---- --
#>     Block position    1  2
#>  Position in block 1, 2  1
#>        learner_key  U3
#>                  B mnr
#>  ----------------- ---
#>     Block position   1
#>  Position in block   1

Multiple within-block positions are comma-separated. Semicolons separate paired block groups when a unit spans several blocks; selecting any reported block position selects the whole unit. The full mapping remains in info.

Choose all values, all non-valid values, or specific blocks in the menu. nonValidValues controls only the second choice: supply numeric codes or text codes as in the example. Its default is c(-99, -98, -97, -96); matching uses original responses, even after revisiting a group. NA responses stay missing. Reset withdraws the group’s previous recoding; no leaves it unchanged.

4. Individual review and resuming

For one decision per person, pass useGroups = NULL explicitly:

result <- visualSubsetRecode(
  dat, info, useGroups = NULL, nonValidValues = c("mbi", "mnr"), toRecodeVal = "mci"
)

All incident rows for a person are combined. For data without classes, use classID = NULL in both checking and preparation; every incident must then name a person, and class-level reports are not allowed.

For longer reviews, choose a new checkpoint file and use the pause menu:

result <- visualSubsetRecode(
  dat, info, nonValidValues = c("mbi", "mnr"),
  toRecodeVal = "mci", checkpoint = "review.rds"
)
# After pausing, including in a later R session:
result <- visualSubsetRecode(state = "review.rds")

Resume with state alone: it retains the original data, decisions and settings, including nonValidValues. Continue processing with result$dat; inspect decisions in result$subsetInfo. For the legacy issues format and all argument details, see prepareSubsetInfo() and visualSubsetRecode().
